title: L4 curation sub-skill — comprehension test agent describes the customization-detection dialog, slot/op decision tree, forbidden-slot refusal, and removal flow from the sub-skill prose alone (PRD-C / Story C10)

questions.question: Read references/sub-skills/common/l4-curation.md. A human says: "For this PR, can the worker double-check the build output before pushing?" A second human says: "From now on, the worker should double-check the build output before pushing." According to the sub-skill, which message activates the l4-curation dialog, which does not, and what specific signals does the agent use to tell them apart?
questions.expected: Only the second message ("From now on, …") activates the l4-curation dialog. The first message ("For this PR, …") is a one-off task and the agent handles it as normal work without writing L4. The signals listed in the 'Activation — customization request detected' and 'Distinguishing a customization request from a one-off task' table: time-horizon language ("always", "from now on", "in this project", "going forward" → durable; "for this task" / "today" / no qualifier → one-off), subject (specific issue/PR/cycle vs. a class of situations), and scope (one role's current action vs. a role's behaviour pattern). The sub-skill also says: if unsure, ASK before assuming durable — one clarifying question is cheaper than a wrongly-written L4 entry.

questions.question: Read references/sub-skills/common/l4-curation.md, especially Step 6 (Pick the file). The human says: "On this project, all the workers should refuse PR descriptions shorter than three sentences." Then later they say: "On this project, no agent ever merges without a CHANGELOG entry." For each directive, which L4 file(s) does the customization land in, and what determines the difference between writing to one file vs. fanning out across many?
questions.expected: The first directive (workers refuse short PR descriptions) is a role-specific customization and lands in a SINGLE file — the role-class the human named, e.g. .squidsquad/project/worker.md (or variant-specific files like worker-frontend.md if the install has worker variants). The second directive (no agent merges without CHANGELOG) is a universal prohibition and fans out across every role-class file — one H3 block is written under the same ## Identity H2 in every role-class's L4 file (pm.md, dm.md, verifier.md, worker.md, etc.), with the wording reused verbatim; only the file placement differs. The difference is determined by whether the customization applies to all roles in the install (universal → fan out) or only to a single named role-class (role-specific → single file). The human is asked to confirm the rule applies team-wide before the fan-out commits.

questions.question: Read references/sub-skills/common/l4-curation.md, especially Step 5 (Pick the op + target). The composed worker CLAUDE.md contains a step with ID `step:cycle/file-bug`. The human says: "Before filing any bug, the worker should scan the incidents/ directory for SEV1 tickets newer than 7 days." Should the agent write this as `### append` or `### insert-before step:cycle/file-bug`, and what general principle from the sub-skill determines that choice?
questions.expected: The agent should write this as `### insert-before step:cycle/file-bug`. The general principle from Step 5: `append` is the safest default for a new rule that doesn't relate to a specific existing step; `insert-before` / `insert-after` is for a new rule that should run ADJACENT TO a specific existing step. The human's directive ("Before filing any bug, …") explicitly anchors the new behaviour to an existing step (file-bug) with a temporal relationship ("before"), so the targeted op is correct. The user-facing question Step 5 frames is "should this happen before or after [existing behaviour]?", not "which op?" — the agent resolves the answer to a real `step:cycle/<step-id>` target without exposing op-name mechanics to the human. (`replace` would be wrong because the existing step's behaviour isn't being replaced — it's being preceded by a pre-check; whole-slot replace is for Responsibility only.)

questions.question: Read references/sub-skills/common/l4-curation.md. The human says: "For this project, the worker should always create a vault note named like `incident-<id>` for every SEV1 bug." Walk through how the sub-skill says the agent should respond, citing the specific rule that governs this case and what alternative path the agent offers the human.
questions.expected: The agent refuses to write this as L4 — the ## Vault slot is L1-exclusive (framework-owned) per COMPOSE-ARCHITECTURE.md §3.3 + §5.6 + §11.2 G4, and compose REJECTS any L4 file containing a ## Vault H2. The sub-skill states this explicitly under Step 2's 'Vault customizations are not L4-authorable at all' callout AND repeats it under Step 5's per-slot op-surface table. The agent explains in plain language (per the 'Talking to the user' rule — never naming SquidSquad internals like 'L1' or 'compose validation') that vault structure is part of SquidSquad's framework, and offers to file an upstream feature request against the SquidSquad repo if the change would be broadly useful. The sub-skill also reinforces this in the 'What this sub-skill does NOT do' section: 'Does NOT cross into vault territory … the vault slot in composed CLAUDE.md is itself L1-exclusive (framework-owned) — l4-curation cannot author it under any circumstances; vault-shaped requests route upstream as feature requests.'

questions.question: Read references/sub-skills/common/l4-curation.md. Several weeks ago the team installed a per-project rule that the worker must run a security smoke test once a week. The human now says: "Forget the weekly security smoke thing — we have a CI job for that now." According to the sub-skill, can the agent silently delete the original H3 block from .squidsquad/project/worker.md? If not, what process does the sub-skill require, and where does the removal-as-a-counter-entry rule appear?
questions.expected: No, the agent CANNOT silently delete the original H3 block. The sub-skill's 'What this sub-skill does NOT do' section states: 'Does NOT prune L4 unilaterally. Any removal goes through the same dialog (confirm with human, then write the removal as a counter-entry per §7.5).' The removal request walks the SAME elicitation dialog as the original customization (durability confirmation, role/scope, why, edge cases, draft + read-back, mini-CQ confirmation, compose dry-run, atomic write/commit/push). The agent then writes the removal as a counter-entry per COMPOSE-ARCHITECTURE.md §7.5 rather than deleting the prior H3 block — this preserves the audit trail (git blame on the L4 file shows BOTH the original directive and the explicit removal directive). The metadata trailer's source-conversation field on the counter-entry quotes the human's removal directive verbatim, so the git log shows the WHY of the undo.

questions.question: Read references/sub-skills/common/l4-curation.md. The human says: "During step:cycle/file-bug, the worker should never reference internal customer names." Why is this NOT authorable as L4, and what does the sub-skill say the agent should do instead?
questions.expected: Step-specific prohibitions ('during step X, do not do Y') do NOT belong in L4. Per COMPOSE-ARCHITECTURE.md §6.3 those live in the relevant L1–L3 sub-skill source — they are built into SquidSquad's shipped behaviour and cannot be overridden per-project. If the human asks for one, the agent explains (in plain language, never naming the layer) that this kind of rule is part of SquidSquad's core, and offers to file an upstream feature request against the SquidSquad repo if the change would be broadly useful. The sub-skill reinforces this in 'What this sub-skill does NOT do': 'Does NOT author step-specific prohibitions as L4. … Route such requests upstream as feature requests against the SquidSquad repo, not into L4.'

questions.question: Read references/sub-skills/common/l4-curation.md Step 8. After the human approves the proposed draft (Step 7), the agent runs four safety gates before the L4 file actually changes on disk. Name the four gates in order, state which Python helper each gate dispatches to, and identify which gate is the single point at which the on-disk file changes.
questions.expected: The four gates in order: (1) DeepSeek decision-tree audit (Gate 1, C3) → l4_audit_gate.py:audit_l4_op(…); (2) Mini-CQ confirmation (Gate 2, C4) → l4_mini_cq.py:format_confirmation + classify_reply; (3) Compose dry-run (Gate 3, C5) → l4_compose_dryrun.py:dryrun_l4(staged_l4_text, role_class); (4) Atomic write + commit + push (Gate 4, C6) → l4_write_commit.py:write_and_commit_l4(…). Gates 1–3 are dry checks (no on-disk change); Gate 4 (C6) is the single point at which the staged text becomes the new L4 file. The sub-skill says: 'Only after all four gates pass is the L4 customization durable. … the file does not change until all four are green, and on any failure between gates the staged text is discarded with no on-disk side effect.'

questions.question: Read references/sub-skills/common/l4-curation.md, especially Step 5 and the 'Agent-internal mapping' table in Step 2. The human says: "Replace the worker's soul entirely with this new personality: relentlessly conservative, never ships without a second pair of eyes." Why does the sub-skill not allow a wholesale replacement of the role's soul via L4, and what op IS available for soul changes?
questions.expected: The ## Soul slot is APPEND-ONLY per COMPOSE-ARCHITECTURE.md §3.3 + §3.4; no targeted ops are legal. Whole-slot replace is NOT supported for Soul. The only legal L4 op against ## Soul is `### append` — composed soul carries shipped content + L4 append in order, and on conflict the agent follows L4 (the L4 append takes precedence at the agent's reading layer per §3.4). So the agent's response: write the directive as a `### append` H3 block under ## Soul in .squidsquad/project/worker.md, surfacing to the human that this LAYERS on top of the existing soul rather than replacing it (the existing soul keywords are still in the agent's composed CLAUDE.md, but L4's append shapes the agent's behaviour where the two conflict). If the human genuinely needs the original soul gone, that is an upstream change to L1–L3, not an L4 customization.

questions.question: Read references/sub-skills/common/l4-curation.md, especially Step 5 and the Responsibility row in Step 2's table. Under what narrow circumstance does the sub-skill say whole-slot `replace` against ## Responsibility is appropriate, and what consequence must the agent surface to the human before using it?
questions.expected: Whole-slot `replace` against ## Responsibility is an escape hatch reserved for the GENUINELY UNUSUAL install case where the entire L1–L3 role contract doesn't apply — the sub-skill's example is 'a single-human project with no DM at all'. Before using whole-slot replace, the agent must surface to the human the consequence: per COMPOSE-ARCHITECTURE.md §5.2, whole-slot replace SILENTLY DISCARDS the entire L1–L3 responsibility block INCLUDING universal team-discipline. The sub-skill explicitly directs the agent to default to `append` (which adds a 'does NOT do' bullet to the role's contract) and to route most boundary tweaks toward `append`. Whole-slot replace is the escape hatch, append is the default.

questions.question: Read references/sub-skills/common/l4-curation.md's 'Talking to the user' section. The agent is mid-dialog with the human and needs to ask which file to write into. State (a) what the agent is allowed to say to the human about file structure, (b) what it is explicitly NOT allowed to say, and (c) what the agent's OWN composed CLAUDE.md is allowed to contain — and why the rule applies to one but not the other.
questions.expected: (a) The agent uses functional descriptions in user-facing prose: "your project's PM agent", "what the role does on each cycle", "the role's personality" — describes the BEHAVIOUR the user sees. The agent asks plain-language functional questions like 'Does this change what the role does each cycle, who the role is, or what the role never does?' (b) The agent NEVER names any SquidSquad concept, component, file, mechanism, or terminology in user-facing prose — no 'slot', 'H2', 'H3', '## Instructions', 'L4', 'compose pipeline', '.squidsquad/project/worker.md', or any name an outside reader would not recognize from the user's own project vocabulary. (c) The agent's OWN composed CLAUDE.md is allowed to freely name sub-skills, slots, ops, file paths — and so is the agent-internal reasoning and the frontmatter in the L4 files it writes. The rule constrains the SPEECH ACT (output addressed to the human), not the agent's cognition. The sub-skill's 'Scope of "user-facing prose"' callout makes this explicit: 'It does NOT include the agent's own composed CLAUDE.md instructions (which freely name sub-skills, slots, ops, file paths), nor agent-internal reasoning, nor the frontmatter in files the agent writes.'

questions.question: Read references/sub-skills/common/l4-curation.md. Does the l4-curation sub-skill run a periodic scan to re-audit existing L4 entries against L1–L3 drift? If not, where is L4-vs-L1-L3 drift caught instead, and what is the sub-skill's stance on that?
questions.expected: No. The sub-skill is one-shot and durable: each customization is captured once via the dialog, written to the right L4 file, and persists across cycles without further intervention. There is no recurring scan over L4 entries. L4-vs-L1–L3 drift is caught at recompose time by the existing dry-run gate (Gate 3, C5, via compose.check_alias_staged_l4 → R1–R7 validation), NOT by a separate curation pass. The sub-skill says this twice — once under 'Purpose' ('L4 curation is one-shot and durable … drift between L4 and L1–L3 is caught at recompose time by the existing dry-run gate, not by a separate curation pass.') and again under 'What this sub-skill does NOT do' ('Does NOT scan or audit existing L4 entries on a recurring schedule. Curation is one-shot per request; entries are durable until the human asks to change them.').
